 Markets Chip stocks slip as Democrats' election sweep clouds the outlook for data centers
 Democrats' wins in Texas and other states raise questions about the AI buildout, while shares of Amazon and Microsoft rose
 By Cris Tolomia · 2 min read · Updated November 4, 2026 Add QZ to Google Austin American-Statesman / Hearst Newspapers / Getty Images
 Micron $MU stock and other chip stocks slipped on Wednesday after Democrats won both chambers of Congress and key governorships, according to projections by The Associated Press, raising questions about the pace of data center construction.
 Nvidia $NVDA stock edged lower in morning trading, and shares of CoreWeave and IREN each fell 4%. Nebius Group stock was down about 0.5%. Oracle $ORCL stock rose 2%, Alphabet $GOOGL stock gained 3%, Amazon $AMZN stock climbed 7%, Meta $META stock rose 2% and Microsoft $MSFT stock added 5.5%.
 Wall Street forecasts hinge on new data center capacity starting operations, according to MarketWatch . The election results cast doubt on where AI infrastructure spending is headed over the longer run, but they do not undo projects with money already committed.
 Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Gov. Greg Abbott $ABT in Texas, according to AP projections. She is calling for data center development in Texas to stop right away, according to CNBC . Wells Fargo $WFC estimates Texas holds 27% of planned U.S. data center gigawatts.
 Democrats also won or retained governorships in Georgia, Pennsylvania and Ohio, according to AP projections. Wells Fargo estimates those states account for 7%, 5% and 5% of planned U.S. data center gigawatts, respectively, according to CNBC.
 In a Wednesday note, Yorkville Ives & Co. partner Dan Ives wrote that the elections will slow data center buildouts across the U.S., according to CNBC. "There is no way to sugarcoat that Democrats taking control especially over the Senate will create some major hurdles for AI and tech legislation in the Beltway over the next 2 years," Ives said. He called the Texas result the "biggest worry" on election night for technology investors.
 Ohsung Kwon, Wells Fargo 's chief equity strategist, wrote in a report this week that a Democratic win in the Texas governor's race could be a "left-tail event" for the AI trade, according to CNBC.
 The Nasdaq $NDAQ -100 entered a correction in late October, with investors increasingly worried that data center spending was expanding more slowly, according to CNBC.
 Broader U.S. stocks moved higher. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 2% after the opening bell as President Donald Trump said he was willing to accept the results . The S&P 500 was up 1.25% and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.3%.
 Hinojosa has campaigned against corporate subsidies and urged a halt to new data center construction. Republicans hold the majority in the Texas Legislature , which limits how much she can change state policy.
